meta.title: Operation of Moisture Balance in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the moisture content of crude drugs and herbal powders by gravimetric loss-on-drying method using an infrared moisture balance.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for standardization of crude drugs — moisture content is a key IP/BP parameter for official drugs.
procedure: Switch on the moisture balance and allow it to warm up for at least 10 minutes before use.
Level the balance using the spirit level and adjusting feet — ensure the balance is perfectly horizontal.
Clean the sample pan with a dry, lint-free cloth and place it on the pan holder.
Tare the pan by pressing the 'Tare' button — the display should read 0.00 g.
Set the drying temperature as per the pharmacopeial requirement for the specific drug: typically 100–105°C for most crude drugs; 60–80°C for heat-sensitive materials.
Set the drying mode: Auto-off (stops when weight change is less than 1 mg in 30 seconds) or timed mode.
Spread approximately 2–5 g of the finely powdered drug sample uniformly across the entire sample pan surface.
Close the lid of the moisture balance to commence heating.
The balance displays weight loss as a percentage in real time.
When drying is complete (auto-stop or timer expires), record the final moisture content displayed.
Open the lid carefully — the sample pan and contents are very hot.
Allow the pan to cool, remove the dry sample, and clean the pan immediately.
Record the sample name, weight taken, temperature used, drying time, and moisture content in the logbook.
Compare the moisture content against pharmacopeial standards (e.g., IP limits).
precautions: Do not overload the sample pan — samples piled too thick dry unevenly giving false low readings.
Spread the sample uniformly across the entire pan area for consistent drying.
Allow the balance to cool completely between successive determinations.
The sample pan and heating element are very hot during and immediately after analysis — use forceps to handle.
Calibrate the moisture balance using a standard substance (e.g., sodium tartrate dihydrate) periodically.
Keep the balance on a stable, vibration-free bench away from drafts.
Do not use for strongly acidic, alkaline, or corrosive materials — they damage the heating element.
